approach-return-by-deadline.reason: It abandons work sooner than configured, needs a reserve policy, and still cannot hold on a busy event loop because the primitive sees only the injected timer; the owner rejected it in the #932 triage.

approach-reserve-option.reason: It widens the frozen Node surface for something a composer already does by passing a smaller deadlineMs, and it would still promise a clock bound the primitive cannot keep.

evidence_ids: the delivery shutdown order test proves the report stays unresolved until the injected deadline timer fires and then counts the settled operation completed and the unsettled one abandoned, failing against a planted drain() that races a real setImmediate; the source check proves delivery-shutdown.ts references no clock or timer global and imports only the timer provider type, failing against planted drain() variants that race a global setTimeout(0), read Date.now() or import setTimeout from node:timers

the README section and the delivery-shutdown.ts doc comments state what deadlineMs bounds, that the report's return is unbounded and the composer's reserve, exactly as the MODIFIED requirement does, with no service level or numeric bound
npm run test:exports reports 19 value and 44 type-only exports, the delivery-shutdown.ts diff changes comments only, and compatibility.json is unchanged

security_justification.audit_integrity: Abandoned work is still never reported delivered; the change states when the abandonment decision is made and pins that the report cannot resolve before it.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No authentication or authorization logic changes; the shutdown primitive gates admission only by lifecycle.
security_justification.authority_provenance: No authority, actor, tenant or commit-state value is read or produced by the shutdown primitive or by this change.
security_justification.concurrency: Admission boundary, in-flight tracking and idempotent shutdown are unchanged; the new tests are sequential, and the accounting defects found here are left to #957 and #958 and not pinned.
security_justification.confidentiality: Documentation, specification, comments and one test; the report carries counts only and the test uses no caller data.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic primitive, hash, signature or key handling is added, removed or changed.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The deadline validation error and every result shape are unchanged; no new diagnostic is added.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No transport, exporter, collector or SIEM integration is added; the timer provider stays injected and host-owned.
security_justification.fail_posture: Outstanding work at the deadline is still counted abandoned, never delivered; the change documents that the report follows that decision rather than bounding it.
security_justification.lifecycle: This is the dimension the change addresses: it states when the shutdown lifecycle decides abandonment and that the report follows it, without changing any lifecycle transition.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Edits are confined to the change directory, the canonical sdk-node spec at fold, the binding's README, comments in delivery-shutdown.ts and its test; no statement of binding source changes.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No privacy transform, field policy or transformation hook is touched.
security_justification.resource_retention: The primitive's in-flight set and its single deadline timer are unchanged; the composer's reserve is a documented host choice, not state retained by the binding.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: No retry or redelivery behaviour changes; abandoned operations' own submit calls still resolve when they settle.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The timer provider stays an injected input; the change places the deadline's timing on the provider explicitly instead of implying a clock the binding does not read.
